the language of “determination” rather than “determinants” has been helpful to our research and related policy/practice efforts in Ecuador and Canada.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the “social” is a critical dimension of health equity and health equity research, and that the language used to describe the social is important.
the language of “health equity” is not sufficient to achieve health equity; rather, it is the language of “determination” of health that can help to advance the field.
